defects: Adds hypothesis `ha0 : a0 ∈ f.support` not present in gold's `UniqueMul` hypothesis; `UniqueMul f.coeff.support g.coeff.support a0 b0` can hold vacuously (no pair a∈supp f, b∈supp g with a*b=a0*b0) without a0 ∈ supp f, so the produced statement excludes cases the gold covers.
Adds hypothesis `hb0 : b0 ∈ g.support` for the same reason — not implied by UniqueMul in the vacuous case.

Uses `[Monoid G]` instead of gold's `[Mul A]`, an unnecessarily strong typeclass assumption (requires associativity and identity) that narrows the class of algebraic structures the theorem applies to compared to the gold, which only needs a `Mul` instance for the monoid-algebra multiplication to be defined.
Adds `[DecidableEq G]`, a hypothesis with no counterpart in the gold statement.
Net effect: the produced theorem is a strictly weaker/special case of the gold theorem (restricted to nonvacuous, monoid, decidable-equality settings) rather than the same general proposition.
